summary: Since about 02:54 UTC (~45 minutes prior), all three go-enricher replicas have been crash-looping in lockstep - each one's memory climbs for 10-20 minutes, then it gets killed and comes back near zero, repeatedly, versus the prior stable cadence of restarting only every 3-4 hours. The enricher never logs a panic or fatal error before a restart, consistent with an OOM kill rather than a handled crash. The Redis-cache-hit debug log line shows a dozen-plus repeats concatenated onto one line before a city name prints, suggesting a buffer or string appended across cache lookups without being reset - a per-transaction memory leak. Throughput on raw_transactions jumped roughly 4x (~1/s to ~4/s) at almost exactly 02:54 UTC, the same moment the crash loop started, which would fill a per-transaction leak faster and explain the shortened restart cadence. Redis was ruled out (healthy throughout, no evictions, no rejected connections, memory flat and low) and go-server was ruled out (error counters flat, transaction counter climbing smoothly).
